metadata.title: How to Use Drizzle ORM with Capacitor and SQLite
metadata.description: Set up Drizzle ORM with Capacitor and SQLite: a working sqlite-proxy driver, typed schema, relational queries, transactions and in-app Drizzle Kit migrations.
metadata.author: Martin Donadieu

faq.question: Does Drizzle ORM support Capacitor?
faq.answer: Drizzle has no Capacitor-specific driver, but its sqlite-proxy driver accepts any async function that runs SQL and returns rows as arrays. Wrapping a Capacitor SQLite plugin in that function gives you the full Drizzle query builder, relational queries and transactions. This guide includes a tested implementation.

faq.question: How do I run Drizzle Kit migrations in a Capacitor app?
faq.answer: Set driver: 'expo' in drizzle.config.ts so Drizzle Kit also writes a migrations.js bundle with the SQL embedded. Import that bundle in the app, make your bundler load .sql files as strings, and apply pending entries at startup with a small migration runner that records applied migrations in a table.

faq.question: Why are some columns undefined or wrong after a join?
faq.answer: Drizzle does not alias joined columns, so two columns with the same name (for example users.id and posts.id) arrive from the plugin as one object key. Select only uniquely named columns, or alias them with sql`${posts.id}`.as('post_id').

faq.question: Which SQLite plugin should I use with Drizzle on Capacitor?
faq.answer: @capacitor-community/sqlite works with the proxy approach because it returns row objects in column order on iOS, Android and web. @capgo/capacitor-fast-sql returns rows keyed by column name without a guaranteed key order on iOS, so for Fast SQL a query builder that reads rows by name, like Kysely, is the better match today.

faq.question: Can I use Drizzle relational queries on mobile?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as you define relations() in the schema and pass the schema to drizzle(). Relational queries use SQLite JSON functions, which are available on iOS and recent Android versions. Test on the oldest Android version you support.
